family: No donor — build the chassis yourself
one_liner: Cheapest in money, most expensive in evenings, and the only route that gives you exactly the window you want.

price.v: £12–20 in materials plus £8–15 for a cage
price.why: Cheaper than a good donor, if you do not count your time.

window_w_mm.why: You are cutting it, so it is whatever you choose. 84 × 27 gives the 256×64 panel a 4 mm border on every side.

chassis.why: Fold to 178 mm wide so the cage's own thickness brings it to 182. Depth is yours to choose, which is the advantage.

cage_included.why: A new ISO 7736 cage is £8–15 and is the one part not worth fabricating.

buttons.v: new tactile switches, exactly where you want them
buttons.why: Six on a ladder, laid out by you rather than by Pioneer in 1999.

knob.v: a new EC11 encoder and any knob you like

display_tech.why: Nothing to gut and nothing to discharge.

why: The window is exactly right, because you cut it to the panel.
The depth is exactly right for your car, because you fold it to fit — which is the one thing no donor can offer.
Nothing to strip, nothing charged, no laser, no thirty-year-old clips to break.
watch_out: It is real metalwork. A bench vice, a folding bar or a sheet of steel and a mallet, and a straight edge you trust.
A hand-cut window in aluminium looks hand-cut. Acrylic is far more forgiving and is what the face should be.
⚠️ Deburr everything. A folded 1 mm edge inside a dashboard is sharp, and you will be reaching past it with a loom in one hand.
steps: Fold the chassis 178 mm wide — the cage takes the remaining 2 mm a side.
Choose the depth from YOUR car's measurement, not from this project's ~160 mm. This is the whole advantage of the route.
Cut the face from 3 mm acrylic, window 84 × 27 for a 256×64 panel.
Back the window with 1 mm smoked acrylic bonded from behind.
Fit new tactile switches and an EC11 to the ladder values in BUILD.md.
Buy the cage. Do not fabricate it — its spring tabs are the one part that has to be right and is cheap to buy.
